mda_name: 542. INSTITUTE OF CHARTERED CHEMISTS OF NIGERIA (ICCON)
mandate_description:

Registers qualified chemists who meet educational and experience requirements. Accredits chemistry degree programs in Nigerian universities ensuring quality training. Conducts professional qualifying examinations for chemists. Issues practicing licenses and enforces continuing professional development. Investigates professional misconduct and enforces disciplinary measures. Promotes chemistry profession development and public awareness. Provides technical advice on chemical safety, quality control and industrial chemistry. Collaborates with chemical industries, universities, research institutes and international chemistry organizations. Addresses challenges from inadequate enforcement, limited public awareness and competing regulatory frameworks. mda_name: 546. INSTITUTE OF FORENSIC SCIENCE LABORATORY, OSHODI
mandate_description:

Located in Oshodi, Lagos State, operating under Federal Ministry of Health or Justice. Established to provide scientific forensic services supporting criminal justice system. Conducts forensic examinations on evidence from crime scenes including DNA analysis, toxicology, ballistics, fingerprints and trace evidence. Provides autopsy and post-mortem examination services for suspicious deaths. Analyzes biological samples including blood, semen, saliva for criminal investigations. Conducts drug analysis identifying illegal substances. Provides forensic toxicology testing for poisons and drug-related deaths. Examines firearms and ballistics evidence. Analyzes document forensics for forgery cases. Trains forensic scientists, pathologists and crime scene investigators. Provides expert testimony in courts. Collaborates with police, security agencies and judiciary. Addresses inadequate forensic capacity nationwide. Faces challenges from equipment shortages, backlog of cases and insufficient forensic professionals. Critical for criminal justice, solving crimes and prosecuting offenders based on scientific evidence.

**Core Mandate:** To provide forensic science services, conduct forensic analysis for criminal investigations, train forensic professionals and support criminal justice system through scientific evidence.

(f) Provide ballistics analysis on firearms and ammunition
(g) Examine fingerprints and palm prints for identification

(i) Conduct blood pattern analysis from crime scenes
(j) Perform forensic serology on biological fluids
(k) Provide document examination for forgery and fraud cases
(l) Conduct forensic pathology determining cause of death
(m) Analyze poison and toxic substance cases
(n) Train forensic scientists and laboratory technicians
(o) Train crime scene investigators on evidence collection
(p) Provide expert witness testimony in criminal trials
(q) Collaborate with Nigeria Police Force on investigations
(r) Coordinate with judiciary on forensic evidence presentation
(s) Maintain forensic evidence chain of custody standards
(t) Advance criminal justice through scientific forensic analysis supporting investigations, prosecutions and convictions based on DNA, toxicology and evidence-based crime solving

mda_name: 547. INSTITUTE OF PUBLIC ANALYSTS OF NIGERIA (IPAN)
mandate_description:

Public analysts examine samples for food quality, drug standards, environmental pollution, water quality and public health. IPAN registers qualified analysts meeting educational and professional requirements. Accredits analytical chemistry programs and laboratory science training. Conducts professional qualifying examinations. Issues practicing licenses to public analysts. Enforces professional conduct and analytical quality standards. Investigates professional misconduct. Provides technical guidance on analytical methods and quality control. Collaborates with NAFDAC, SON, environmental agencies and regulatory bodies. Addresses food safety, drug quality and environmental monitoring through professional analytical services. Promotes laboratory accreditation and good laboratory practices. mda_name: 548. INTERCOUNTRY CENTRE FOR ORAL HEALTH (ICOH), JOS

Provides specialized dental services including maxillofacial surgery, orthodontics and prosthodontics. Trains dentists, dental therapists and oral health workers from Nigeria and West African countries. Conducts community oral health programs promoting dental hygiene and preventive care. Researches traditional oral health practices and dental disease patterns in Africa. Develops oral health policies and guidelines for West African region. Collaborates with WHO, dental schools and international oral health organizations. Addresses inadequate dental specialists and poor oral health in region. Investment and Securities Tribunal (IST) is specialized judicial tribunal adjudicating disputes in Nigeria's capital market and securities industry. Located in Abuja with Lagos and Port Harcourt divisions, operating under Investments and Securities Act as independent tribunal. Established to provide fast-track resolution of capital market disputes avoiding lengthy regular court proceedings. IST hears cases involving securities transactions, capital market operations, stockbrokers' conduct, insider trading, market manipulation and investment fraud. Adjudicates disputes between investors and stockbrokers, companies and shareholders, and regulatory compliance issues. Tribunal comprises judges with securities law expertise. Conducts hearings, examines evidence and issues judgments enforceable like High Court orders. Appeals go to Court of Appeal. Provides specialized expertise in complex securities matters. Addresses market abuse, investor protection and regulatory enforcement. Promotes investor confidence through effective dispute resolution. Faces challenges from limited public awareness, jurisdictional overlaps with regular courts and case backlogs. Complements Securities and Exchange Commission regulatory enforcement. Critical for capital market integrity and investor protection.

Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (ISTH) Irrua is specialized federal tertiary hospital and teaching institution. Located in Irrua, Edo State in south-south Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Health and affiliated with Ambrose Alli University. Established as specialist hospital focusing on infectious diseases, particularly Lassa fever for which it houses Nigeria's premier Lassa fever treatment center. ISTH is national reference center for viral hemorrhagic fevers including Lassa fever endemic in southern Nigeria. Provides specialized treatment for Lassa fever with isolation facilities and trained staff. Conducts research on Lassa fever epidemiology, treatment and prevention. Offers general tertiary healthcare services including surgery, internal medicine, obstetrics and pediatrics. Provides postgraduate medical training for doctors. Trains healthcare workers on Lassa fever management and infection control. Collaborates with WHO, CDC, NCDC and international partners on viral hemorrhagic fever response. Serves as epidemic response center during Lassa fever outbreaks. Operates virology laboratory conducting diagnostic testing. Critical for Nigeria's Lassa fever control and infectious disease preparedness. Addresses annual Lassa fever epidemics affecting southern Nigeria.

Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) is federal examination body conducting entrance examinations and managing admissions into Nigerian tertiary institutions. Headquartered in Abuja with offices nationwide, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. JAMB registers candidates for UTME annually with over 1.8 million candidates. Conducts computer-based UTME testing nationwide. Sets minimum admission requirements (cutoff marks) for tertiary institutions. Manages Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) where institutions admit students. Conducts Direct Entry examinations for candidates with advanced qualifications. Regulates admission processes preventing illegal admissions. Promotes merit-based admissions. Introduces policies like uniform cutoff marks and CAPS transparency. Faces challenges from examination malpractice, technical glitches, admission racketeering and tertiary institutions' non-compliance. Remits proceeds to Federal Government. Kainji National Park is federal protected area conserving biodiversity and wildlife in northwestern Nigeria. Located across Niger, Kwara and Kebbi States covering approximately 5,341 square kilometers in two sectors (Borgu and Zugurma), operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Established in 1979 following creation of Kainji Dam and Lake Kainji requiring wildlife conservation. The park protects savanna ecosystems, woodland and grassland habitats. Houses significant wildlife including elephants, hippopotamus, buffalo, various antelopes (roan, kob, hartebeest), lions, leopards, baboons and over 350 bird species. Borgu sector adjoins Benin's W National Park forming transboundary conservation complex. Faces threats from poaching, cattle grazing, illegal fishing in park waters and human encroachment. Tourism infrastructure limited but includes game viewing and safari camps. Park management involves anti-poaching patrols, habitat conservation, community engagement and sustainable tourism. Collaborates with Benin and Niger on transboundary wildlife conservation. Critical for northwestern Nigeria biodiversity protection and eco-tourism potential.

**Core Mandate:** To protect and conserve wildlife and ecosystems, manage sustainable tourism, conduct conservation research and promote environmental education in northwestern Nigeria.

Kamuku National Park is federal protected area conserving biodiversity and ecosystems in northwestern Nigeria. Located in Kaduna and Niger States covering approximately 1,121 square kilometers, operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Established to protect forest and savanna ecosystems in northwestern Nigeria. The park preserves gallery forests, woodland savanna and grassland habitats. Houses wildlife including various antelopes, monkeys, baboons, hyenas and bird species. Protects water catchment areas for rivers feeding communities. Faces severe threats from illegal logging, charcoal production, poaching, farmland encroachment and gold mining activities destroying habitats. Mining activities particularly damaging with illegal miners operating within park. Park management severely constrained by limited resources, inadequate rangers and encroachment pressure from surrounding communities. Requires urgent intervention preventing total degradation. mda_name: 557. LAGOS INTERNATIONAL TRADE FAIR COMPLEX MANAGEMENT BOARD
mandate_description:

Located in Badagry Expressway, Lagos State, operating under Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. Established to manage Lagos International Trade Fair Complex hosting annual Lagos International Trade Fair and commercial exhibitions. Hosts annual Lagos International Trade Fair attracting thousands of exhibitors and visitors showcasing products, services and business opportunities. Generates revenue from exhibition space rentals and event hosting. Promotes Nigerian products and "Made in Nigeria" campaigns. Facilitates business networking and trade connections. Lagos Liaison Office is Federal Government's administrative office maintaining federal presence in Lagos, Nigeria's commercial capital. Located in Lagos State, operating under Office of Secretary to Government of the Federation or relevant federal ministry. Coordinates federal agencies' Lagos operations and activities. Facilitates federal government business in commercial capital. Manages federal government properties and assets in Lagos. Provides liaison services for federal officials visiting Lagos. Coordinates with Lagos State Government on federal-state matters. Supports federal government events and programs in Lagos. Manages protocol for federal dignitaries. Facilitates federal government procurement and logistics in Lagos. Represents federal interests in commercial capital. Lagos remains Nigeria's commercial center despite Abuja being political capital, requiring federal coordination presence. Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) is premier federal tertiary healthcare institution and teaching hospital. Located in Idi-Araba, Lagos State, operating under Federal Ministry of Health and affiliated with University of Lagos (UNILAG). Operates multiple specialties including surgery, internal medicine, obstetrics/gynecology, pediatrics, cardiology, oncology, neurosurgery, nephrology and others. Serves as major referral hospital for Lagos State (population ~20 million) and southwestern Nigeria. Provides postgraduate medical training through robust residency programs training specialists. Trains UNILAG medical students during clinical years. Conducts extensive clinical research. Operates one of Nigeria's busiest accident and emergency departments. Provides cancer treatment, cardiac surgery, kidney transplant and other advanced services. Faces challenges from overwhelming patient load, inadequate funding, aging infrastructure and periodic healthcare worker strikes. Lake Chad Research Institute (LCRI) Maiduguri is federal agricultural research institution conducting research on Lake Chad Basin agriculture, fisheries and natural resources. Located in Maiduguri, Borno State in northeastern Nigeria, operating under Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria and Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Established to address agricultural and environmental challenges in Lake Chad Basin agroecological zone. Conducts research on crops adapted to semi-arid Lake Chad region including sorghum, millet, cowpea, groundnut and wheat. Researches irrigation farming and water management for Lake Chad waters. Conducts fisheries research on Lake Chad fish species, fishing practices and aquaculture. Researches livestock production in pastoral communities. Studies Lake Chad shrinkage impacts on agriculture and livelihoods. Develops climate-resilient farming systems for Sahel environment. Researches flood recession agriculture practiced around Lake Chad. Provides technical advice on Lake Chad Basin management. Legal Aid Council of Nigeria is federal agency providing free legal services to indigent citizens who cannot afford legal representation. Headquartered in Abuja with offices in all 36 states and FCT, operating under Federal Ministry of Justice per Legal Aid Act 2011. Operates Legal Aid clinics in courts, prisons and communities. Represents accused persons facing serious criminal charges who cannot afford lawyers. Provides legal services in civil matters including land disputes, family law, employment and consumer rights. Offers legal advice and counseling to indigent citizens. Conducts public legal education and awareness programs. Provides legal services to women, children, persons with disabilities and vulnerable groups. Operates paralegal training programs. Collaborates with NBA, law firms and pro bono lawyers. Means-tests applicants to determine eligibility based on income. mda_name: 563. LOWER BENUE RIVER BASIN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (LBRBDA)
mandate_description:
Lower Benue River Basin Development Authority (LBRBDA) is federal agency managing water resources, irrigation and agricultural development in Lower Benue River Basin. Headquartered in Makurdi covering Benue, Kogi, Nasarawa, Cross River, Ebonyi, Enugu and Anambra States, operating under Federal Ministry of Water Resources. Established as one of Nigeria's 12 River Basin Development Authorities. The basin includes Lower Benue River and tributaries. LBRBDA develops irrigation schemes supporting dry season farming. Constructs and operates small/medium dams for irrigation water supply. Manages water distribution to farmers and communities. Supports rice, vegetables and yam production through irrigation. Provides flood control infrastructure. Conducts hydrological studies and water resources assessment. Develops fadama (floodplain) irrigation exploiting seasonal water availability. Provides agricultural extension services to irrigated farmers. Faces challenges from flooding (Benue experiences major floods), inadequate infrastructure maintenance and farmer participation. Benue River's significant discharge creates both irrigation opportunities and flood risks requiring integrated management.

Maritime Academy of Nigeria Oron is premier federal maritime training institution providing education for seafarers and maritime professionals. Located in Oron, Akwa Ibom State in coastal south-south Nigeria, operating under Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) and Federal Ministry of Transportation. Established in 1977 to train Nigerian seafarers, marine engineers, nautical officers and maritime professionals. Offers certificate, diploma and degree programs in nautical science, marine engineering, maritime transport and related fields. Provides Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) compliant training meeting International Maritime Organization (IMO) requirements. Trains deck officers (navigators), marine engineers, electro-technical officers and ratings. Operates training vessels for practical sea-going experience. Provides simulator training for navigation, engine room and ship handling. Offers specialized courses in ship security, survival at sea and marine operations. Trains for merchant navy careers. Collaborates with IMO, international maritime academies and shipping companies. Addresses shortage of qualified Nigerian seafarers in global shipping industry. Cabotage Act implementation increases demand for Nigerian seafarers. Faces challenges from inadequate vessels, equipment maintenance and international certification requirements.

mda_name: 566. MEDICAL AND DENTAL COUNCIL OF NIGERIA (MDCN)
mandate_description:
Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) is statutory regulatory body overseeing medical and dental professions. Headquartered in Abuja, operating under MDCN Act as independent regulatory authority. Established to regulate medical doctors, dentists and ensure professional standards protecting public health. Registers qualified medical practitioners and dentists. Accredits medical and dental schools ensuring quality training. Conducts professional examinations for foreign-trained doctors. mda_name: 570. MICHAEL IMODU INSTITUTE OF LABOUR STUDIES
mandate_description:
Michael Imodu Institute of Labour Studies is federal training and research institution for labor studies, industrial relations and trade unionism. Located in Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment. Named after Michael Imoudu, prominent Nigerian labor leader. Established to provide training, research and capacity building for labor movement, trade unions and industrial relations practitioners. Conducts training programs for trade union leaders, shop stewards and labor organizers. Provides industrial relations education for employers, workers and government officials. Conducts research on labor issues, collective bargaining, workers' rights and employment relations. Offers certificate and diploma programs in labor studies. Trains labor inspectors and ministry of labour officials. Provides negotiation and conflict resolution skills training. Conducts workers' education promoting labor rights awareness. Researches Nigerian labor history and trade union movements. Collaborates with ILO, trade unions (NLC, TUC) and international labor education institutions. Addresses challenges from declining union membership, changing work patterns and labor movement fragmentation. Critical for industrial harmony, collective bargaining effectiveness and workers' rights protection.

mda_name: 571. MICHAEL OKPARA UNIVERSITY OF AGRICULTURE, UMUDIKE (MOUAU)
mandate_description:
Michael Okpara University of Agriculture Umudike (MOUAU) is specialized federal university focusing on agricultural education, research and development. Located in Umudike, Abia State in southeastern Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. Established in 1992 and named after Dr. Michael Okpara, former Premier of Eastern Nigeria and agricultural champion. MOUAU focuses exclusively on agriculture, agricultural sciences and related disciplines. Offers undergraduate and postgraduate programs in agronomy, animal science, soil science, agricultural economics, agricultural engineering, food science, forestry and fisheries. Conducts agricultural research on crop production, livestock, soil management and agricultural technologies. Operates teaching and research farms demonstrating improved agricultural practices. Focuses on southeastern Nigeria agroecological zone crops including cassava, yam, cocoa, oil palm and vegetables. Conducts extension services training farmers. Researches sustainable agriculture, climate-smart farming and agricultural mechanization. Collaborates with IITA, agricultural research institutes and international agricultural universities. Addresses food security, rural development and agricultural transformation. Produces agricultural graduates and expertise supporting Nigeria's agricultural sector development.

Military Pension Board is federal agency managing pensions and retirement benefits for Nigerian Armed Forces personnel. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Defence. Established to administer pension payments, gratuities and death benefits for retired military personnel, veterans and dependents of deceased service members. Processes retirement benefits for Army, Navy and Air Force retirees. Calculates pension entitlements based on rank, years of service and retirement conditions. Pays monthly pensions to retired military personnel. Processes gratuities (lump sum retirement benefits) upon discharge. Manages death benefits and pensions for widows/orphans of deceased soldiers. Addresses pension arrears and outstanding payments. Maintains database of military retirees and pensioners. Verifies pensioners through biometric registration preventing fraud. Collaborates with Defense Headquarters, service branches and PenCom. Faces challenges from pension arrears, inadequate funding, verification difficulties and delayed payments affecting veterans' welfare. Military pension is distinct from contributory pension applying to civilian workers. Critical for military morale, retirement security and honoring service to nation.

**Core Mandate:** To administer military pensions, pay retirement benefits, manage gratuities and death benefits, and ensure welfare of retired armed forces personnel and dependents.

Mining Cadastral Office (MCO) is federal agency managing mining rights, mineral titles and mining cadastre system. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development. Established to administer transparent allocation of mineral exploration and mining rights. MCO operates online Mining Cadastre Portal implementing "first-come-first-served" principle for mineral title applications. Issues mineral exploration licenses, mining leases, small-scale mining licenses and quarrying permits. Maintains comprehensive database of all mineral titles across Nigeria. Prevents overlapping claims through geographic information system (GIS) mapping. Processes applications for mineral rights electronically. Monitors compliance with mineral title conditions. Collects royalties and fees from mining license holders. Provides transparency in mineral rights allocation preventing corruption. Makes mineral title information publicly accessible. Collaborates with mining companies, artisanal miners and state governments. Addresses challenges from illegal mining, artisanal mining formalization and mineral revenue collection. Critical for mining sector regulation, investor confidence and transparent mineral resource governance. Supports Nigeria's solid minerals sector development beyond oil dependence.

**Core Mandate:** To administer mineral rights, issue mining licenses, manage mining cadastre, ensure transparent allocation and regulate mining title system in Nigeria.

Federal Ministry of Defence Headquarters is apex civilian ministry overseeing Nigerian Armed Forces and defense policy. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Defence appointed by President. Provides civilian oversight and political direction for military. Formulates national defense policy and military strategy. Coordinates Army, Navy, Air Force and Defense Intelligence Agency. Manages defense budget allocation across service branches. Oversees procurement of military equipment, weapons and platforms. Supervises military operations against Boko Haram, banditry and insurgency. Coordinates defense diplomacy and military cooperation with foreign countries. Manages defense industries and military production. Oversees military training institutions. Coordinates peacekeeping troop contributions to UN and AU missions. Supervises veterans' affairs and military welfare. Coordinates civil-military relations. Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs Headquarters is apex ministry managing Nigeria's foreign policy, diplomacy and international relations. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Foreign Affairs appointed by President. Formulates and implements Nigeria's foreign policy. Conducts treaty negotiations and international agreements. Protects Nigerian citizens abroad through consular services. Promotes Nigeria's economic diplomacy and trade interests. Coordinates development cooperation and foreign aid. Manages diaspora engagement policies. Oversees protocol for foreign dignitaries visiting Nigeria. Federal Ministry of Interior is ministry overseeing internal security agencies, immigration, prisons and civil defense. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Interior appointed by President. Supervises Nigeria Immigration Service controlling borders and immigration. Manages Federal Fire Service for firefighting and emergency response. Formulates policies on internal security, immigration, corrections and civil protection. Coordinates border management and immigration control. Oversees prison reforms and correctional rehabilitation programs. Manages national identity cards and civil registration. Coordinates disaster management and emergency response. Supervises passport issuance and visa policies. Federal Ministry of Petroleum Resources is apex ministry overseeing Nigeria's oil and gas industry and petroleum sector. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Petroleum Resources (often held by President) and Minister of State. Formulates petroleum policies and regulations. Supervises NNPC Ltd (Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited). Regulates upstream oil exploration and production. Oversees downstream petroleum refining and distribution. Negotiates Production Sharing Contracts with international oil companies. Manages Nigeria's OPEC participation and oil production quotas. mda_name: 578. MODIBBO ADAMA UNIVERSITY TEACHING HOSPITAL (MAUTH), YOLA
mandate_description:
Modibbo Adama University Teaching Hospital Yola is federal tertiary healthcare institution and teaching hospital. Located in Yola, Adamawa State in northeastern Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Health and affiliated with Modibbo Adama University (formerly Adamawa State University renamed federal university). Provides postgraduate medical training for doctors pursuing specialist qualifications. Trains medical students from Modibbo Adama University during clinical rotations. Conducts clinical research on health challenges in northeastern Nigeria. Operates in region affected by Boko Haram insurgency managing conflict-related injuries and displaced populations' health needs. Provides maternal and child healthcare. National Assembly Management is administrative arm supporting Nigeria's bicameral legislature. Located in Abuja at National Assembly Complex, operating under National Assembly Service Commission. Federal Technical College Uromi, Edo State, is a federal technical college providing technical and vocational secondary education. Located in Uromi, Edo State in south-south Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. Uromi is major town in Esan region of Edo State. Federal Technical College Zuru, Kebbi State, is a federal technical college providing technical and vocational secondary education. Located in Zuru, Kebbi State in northwestern Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. Zuru is town and Local Government headquarters in Kebbi State. Kebbi State is predominantly agricultural state known for rice production and fishing. Gashaka Gumti National Park is Nigeria's largest national park protecting biodiversity, wildlife and ecosystems. Located across Taraba and Adamawa States in northeastern Nigeria covering approximately 6,731 square kilometers, operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Established in 1991 by merging Gashaka and Gumti Game Reserves creating Nigeria's premier wildlife conservation area. The park protects montane forests, savanna, grasslands and Nigeria's highest mountain peak (Chappal Waddi at 2,419 meters). Houses significant biodiversity including chimpanzees, elephants, buffalo, hippopotamus, various antelopes, lions (possibly), leopards and over 500 bird species. Provides critical watershed for Taraba and Benue Rivers. Faces threats from poaching, illegal logging, cattle grazing encroachment and human-wildlife conflict. Tourism potential largely undeveloped due to remoteness and infrastructure challenges. Park management involves conservation, anti-poaching patrols, research, community engagement and sustainable tourism development. Collaborates with local communities on conservation and livelihood programs.

**Core Mandate:** To protect and conserve Nigeria's biodiversity, wildlife and ecosystems; manage sustainable tourism; conduct conservation research; and promote environmental education in Nigeria's largest national park.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Protect and conserve biodiversity in Nigeria's largest national park covering 6,731 square kilometers
(b) Safeguard endangered and threatened wildlife species including chimpanzees and elephants
(c) Preserve montane forest, savanna and grassland ecosystems
(d) Conduct anti-poaching patrols and law enforcement against illegal hunting
(e) Combat illegal logging and forest destruction within park boundaries
(f) Manage human-wildlife conflict with surrounding communities
(g) Protect critical watershed for Taraba and Benue Rivers
(h) Conduct conservation research on wildlife populations and ecosystem health
(i) Monitor and track wildlife including chimpanzees, elephants and large mammals
(j) Develop and manage sustainable ecotourism infrastructure
(k) Provide environmental education programs for schools and communities
(l) Engage local communities in conservation through participatory approaches
(m) Develop alternative livelihoods reducing pressure on park resources
(n) Manage park infrastructure including ranger stations and tourist facilities
(o) Collaborate with international conservation organizations on biodiversity protection
(p) Control illegal cattle grazing encroachment destroying park vegetation
(q) Maintain park boundaries and prevent encroachment
(r) Conduct biodiversity surveys and ecological monitoring
(s) Promote Nigeria's natural heritage and environmental conservation
(t) Advance Nigeria's biodiversity conservation, protect critical ecosystems and support sustainable development in northeastern Nigeria through Africa's important Afromontane forest protection

Geneva Labour Desk Office is specialized Nigerian government office representing Nigeria's labor interests at International Labour Organization (ILO) and UN agencies in Geneva, Switzerland. Located in Geneva, Switzerland alongside Nigeria's Foreign Mission to UN/international organizations, operating under Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment. Geneva hosts ILO headquarters, primary UN agency addressing labor standards, workers' rights, employment and social protection globally. The office coordinates Nigeria's participation in ILO activities including International Labour Conferences, technical meetings, standard-setting conventions and programs. Represents Nigerian workers, employers and government in tripartite ILO structure. Monitors international labor standards adoption and reports on Nigeria's compliance. Facilitates ILO technical assistance to Nigeria on employment policies, labor legislation, occupational safety and social security. Engages on child labor, forced labor, freedom of association and discrimination issues affecting Nigerian workers. Coordinates with Nigerian missions, labor unions and employers' organizations. Advocates Nigerian positions on global labor issues.

**Core Mandate:** To represent Nigeria's labor interests at International Labour Organization, coordinate ILO engagement, advocate workers' rights, facilitate technical assistance and advance Nigerian labor agenda in global labor governance.

**Statutory Functions:**

(q) Coordinate with Nigerian labor unions and employers' organizations
(r) Participate in ILO technical meetings and expert committees
(s) Advocate Nigerian positions on global labor governance
(t) Advance Nigeria's labor agenda in ILO promoting decent work, workers' rights and social justice globally

Geological Survey of Nigeria (GSN) is premier federal geological research institution conducting geological surveys, mineral exploration, geoscience research and providing geological information. Headquartered in Abuja with offices nationwide, operating under Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development. Established to systematically map Nigeria's geology, identify mineral resources and provide geoscience data for national development. GSN conducts geological mapping at various scales, geochemical and geophysical surveys, mineral exploration and assessment. Maintains National Geoscience Data Repository holding geological maps, borehole data, geochemical samples and mineral information. Provides technical advice on mining, groundwater, engineering geology, environmental geology and natural hazards. Conducts research on earthquakes, landslides, erosion and geological hazards. Supports mining sector through pre-feasibility studies and mineral potential assessments. Collaborates with universities, international geological surveys and mining companies. Produces and distributes geological maps, reports and databases. Faces challenges from inadequate funding, equipment obsolescence and competition from private sector geological services.

**Core Mandate:** To conduct geological surveys and mapping, explore and assess mineral resources, provide geoscience information, and support mining sector development and national geological knowledge.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Conduct systematic geological mapping of Nigeria at various scales (1:50,000 to 1:1,000,000)
(b) Explore and assess Nigeria's mineral resources including metallic and industrial minerals
(c) Conduct geochemical surveys identifying mineralized zones and geochemical anomalies
(d) Perform geophysical surveys using magnetic, electromagnetic and seismic methods
(e) Maintain National Geoscience Data Repository and geological databases

Hadejia-Jama'are River Basin Development Authority (HJRBDA) is federal agency managing water resources, irrigation development and agricultural programs in Hadejia-Jama'are river basin. Headquartered in Kano covering Kano, Jigawa, Yobe and Bauchi States in northern Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Water Resources. Established as one of Nigeria's 12 River Basin Development Authorities managing basin water resources. The basin includes Hadejia and Jama'are Rivers flowing into Lake Chad supporting extensive wetlands including Hadejia-Nguru wetlands. HJRBDA develops irrigation schemes, constructs dams, manages water distribution and supports dry season farming. Operates Tiga and Challawa Gorge Dams on Kano River providing irrigation water and flood control. Develops small and medium irrigation schemes for rice, wheat and vegetable production. Manages Hadejia-Nguru wetlands important for fishing, farming and biodiversity. Faces challenges from competing water uses, upstream dam impacts on downstream wetlands, climate variability and inadequate infrastructure maintenance. Supports rice production in Kano-Jigawa-Yobe irrigation schemes.

(c) Construct, operate and maintain Tiga and Challawa Gorge Dams

(h) Provide flood control and water storage services

(k) Support fisheries in reservoirs and wetlands
(l) Provide agricultural extension services to irrigated farmers

(p) Collaborate with State governments on irrigation development

(s) Adapt to climate variability affecting water availability
(t) Advance irrigation agriculture, water security and wetland conservation supporting rice production and livelihoods in northern Nigeria's critical agricultural basin

Health Records Registration Board is statutory regulatory body overseeing health records and health information management profession in Nigeria. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Health. Established to regulate health information management practitioners ensuring professional standards in medical records, health information systems and data management across healthcare facilities. The Board registers qualified health records officers, accredits health information management training programs and enforces professional conduct standards. (o) Collaborate with hospitals on improving records management systems
(p) Promote patient data privacy and confidentiality standards
(q) Support health research through quality health data management

mda_name: 533. INDEPENDENT CORRUPT PRACTICES AND RELATED OFFENCES COMMISSION (ICPC)
mandate_description:
Independent Corrupt Practices and Related Offences Commission (ICPC) is federal anti-corruption agency investigating, preventing and prosecuting corruption in public sector. Headquartered in Abuja with zonal offices nationwide, operating as independent statutory body under ICPC Act 2000. Established to combat corruption complementing Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). ICPC focuses on corruption prevention, public sector corruption, abuse of office, gratification and system reforms strengthening integrity. Investigates corruption allegations against public officials including bribery, fraud, abuse of office and illicit enrichment. Prosecutes corruption cases in courts. Conducts Corruption Risk Assessments and System Study Reviews identifying corruption vulnerabilities in MDAs. Promotes ethics, integrity and anti-corruption education. Monitors Constituency Projects and capital releases tracking implementation. Receives and investigates petitions from citizens. Operates independently though faces challenges from political interference, inadequate funding, lengthy prosecutions and weak conviction rates. Collaborates with EFCC, CCB, CCT and international anti-corruption agencies.

**Core Mandate:** To prevent, investigate and prosecute corruption in public sector; strengthen integrity systems; promote ethics; and advance anti-corruption reforms in Nigeria.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Investigate corruption, bribery and abuse of office allegations in public sector
(b) Prosecute corrupt public officials in courts for corruption offenses
(c) Prevent corruption through system reforms and integrity strengthening
(d) Conduct Corruption Risk Assessments in Ministries, Departments and Agencies
(e) Perform System Study Reviews identifying corruption vulnerabilities
(f) Monitor Constituency Projects and capital releases tracking fund utilization
(g) Receive, investigate and act on corruption petitions from citizens
(h) Investigate gratification, bribery and illicit enrichment by public officials
(i) Prosecute abuse of office, fraud and corruption in procurement
(j) Promote ethics, integrity and anti-corruption values in public service
(k) Conduct anti-corruption education in schools, MDAs and communities
(l) Enforce asset declaration requirements for public officials
(m) Collaborate with EFCC on joint anti-corruption operations
(n) Coordinate with Code of Conduct Bureau on asset verification
(o) Provide technical assistance to MDAs on corruption prevention
(p) Conduct public enlightenment campaigns on corruption reporting
(q) Collaborate with civil society organizations on anti-corruption advocacy
(r) Coordinate with international anti-corruption agencies and conventions
(s) Recommend policy and legislative reforms strengthening anti-corruption frameworks
(t) Advance Nigeria's anti-corruption fight through prevention, investigation, prosecution and systemic reforms reducing corruption in public institutions

Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is Nigeria's electoral management body conducting elections, voter registration and electoral processes. Headquartered in Abuja with offices in all 36 states and 774 Local Governments, operating as constitutionally established independent commission. Mandated by 1999 Constitution and Electoral Act to organize, conduct and supervise elections for President, National Assembly, Governors and State Assemblies. INEC registers voters through Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) maintaining national voter register. Conducts elections including presidential, gubernatorial, National Assembly, State Assembly and Area Council elections. Registers political parties and monitors party activities. Delimits constituencies for electoral purposes. Conducts voter education promoting electoral participation. Procures electoral materials including ballot papers, result sheets and Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) technology. Recruits and trains ad hoc election staff. Announces election results and issues Certificates of Return to winners. Faces challenges from electoral violence, logistical difficulties, result manipulation allegations, voter apathy and political interference despite constitutional independence.

**Core Mandate:** To organize, conduct and supervise free, fair and credible elections; register voters and political parties; promote electoral participation; and strengthen Nigeria's democracy through professional electoral management.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Organize, conduct and supervise presidential elections every four years
(b) Conduct National Assembly elections for Senate and House of Representatives
(c) Organize gubernatorial elections in 36 states
(d) Conduct State Houses of Assembly elections across Nigeria
(e) Organize Area Council elections in Federal Capital Territory
(f) Register eligible Nigerian citizens as voters through Continuous Voter Registration
(g) Maintain and update National Register of Voters
(h) Register political parties meeting constitutional requirements
(i) Monitor political party activities and campaign finances
(j) Delimit constituencies for National Assembly and State Assemblies
(k) Conduct voter education and public enlightenment on electoral processes
(l) Procure electoral materials including ballot papers and result sheets
(m) Deploy Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for voter authentication
(n) Recruit, train and deploy ad hoc election staff including Presiding Officers
(o) Collate and announce election results at ward, LGA, state and national levels
(p) Issue Certificates of Return to elected officials
(q) Address electoral offenses including vote buying and ballot stuffing
(r) Conduct bye-elections and re-run elections as ordered by courts
(s) Collaborate with security agencies on election security
(t) Advance Nigeria's democracy through credible electoral processes, transparent result management and continuous electoral reforms strengthening public confidence in democratic governance

Industrial Arbitration Panel (IAP) is specialized tribunal adjudicating industrial disputes between employers and workers in Nigeria. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment per Trade Disputes Act. Established to resolve industrial disputes through arbitration avoiding prolonged strikes disrupting economy. IAP hears trade disputes referred by Minister of Labour when conciliation fails. Adjudicates disputes on wages, conditions of employment, termination, unfair labor practices and collective bargaining disagreements. Panel comprises neutral arbitrators with labor law expertise. Conducts hearings, examines evidence, hears parties and issues binding awards. Awards are enforceable in National Industrial Court. Provides faster dispute resolution than courts. Addresses disputes in critical sectors including oil/gas, banking, aviation, health and education. Promotes industrial harmony and peaceful labor relations. Faces challenges from parties' non-compliance with awards, legal challenges to jurisdiction and limited enforcement mechanisms. Complements National Industrial Court and labor ministry conciliation services.

**Core Mandate:** To adjudicate industrial disputes through arbitration, issue binding awards, promote industrial harmony and resolve employer-worker conflicts in Nigerian labor market.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Adjudicate industrial disputes referred by Minister of Labour and Employment
(b) Hear trade disputes between employers and workers/unions
(c) Arbitrate disputes on wages, salaries and remuneration
(d) Resolve conflicts over conditions of employment and workplace rights
(e) Adjudicate wrongful termination and unfair dismissal disputes
(f) Address unfair labor practices by employers or unions
(g) Resolve collective bargaining disagreements
(h) Conduct arbitration hearings in industrial dispute cases
(i) Examine evidence, witness testimonies and parties' submissions
(j) Issue binding arbitration awards resolving disputes
(k) Enforce awards through National Industrial Court mechanisms
(l) Prevent or end strikes through binding dispute resolution
(m) Promote industrial peace and harmonious labor relations
(n) Address disputes in critical sectors (oil/gas, banking, aviation, health)
(o) Provide expedited alternative to lengthy court litigation
(p) Protect workers' rights while balancing employers' interests
(q) Interpret collective agreements and employment contracts
(r) Coordinate with Ministry of Labour on labor dispute management
(s) Collaborate with National Industrial Court on enforcement
(t) Advance industrial harmony, prevent disruptive strikes and resolve employer-worker conflicts protecting Nigeria's economic stability and workers' rights

Industrial Training Fund (ITF) is premier federal skills development agency providing vocational training, skills acquisition and human capital development for Nigerian workforce. Headquartered in Jos, Plateau State with Area Offices and Model Skills Training Centres nationwide, operating under Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. Established by ITF Act 2011 to promote acquisition of skills in industry and commerce. ITF collects 1% levy from companies with 5+ employees (payroll ≥N50 million annually) financing training programs. Provides skills training in technical trades, industrial skills, entrepreneurship and modern technologies. Operates Model Skills Training Centres offering courses in welding, electrical, automotive, construction, ICT and other trades. Reimburses companies' training costs through levy rebate system. Conducts National Industrial Skills Development Programme (NISDP). Offers entrepreneurship training for unemployed youth. Provides Train-the-Trainer programs for instructors. Conducts apprenticeship programs linking trainees with employers. Addresses youth unemployment, skills mismatch and inadequate technical workforce. Collaborates with industries, training institutions and international skills development agencies.

**Core Mandate:** To promote skills acquisition, provide vocational training, develop industrial workforce, support entrepreneurship and reduce unemployment through comprehensive skills development programs.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Promote acquisition of industrial, technical and vocational skills across sectors
(b) Collect 1% training levy from companies with 5+ employees for training funding
(c) Administer levy rebate scheme reimbursing companies' approved training costs
(d) Operate Model Skills Training Centres providing practical vocational training
(e) Conduct National Industrial Skills Development Programme (NISDP)
(f) Provide skills training in welding, fabrication, electrical and mechanical trades
(g) Offer automotive mechanics, building construction and plumbing training
(h) Conduct ICT, computer and digital skills training programs
(i) Provide entrepreneurship training for unemployed youth and graduates
(j) Conduct Train-the-Trainer programs for vocational instructors
(k) Organize apprenticeship programs linking trainees with industries
(l) Provide on-the-job training and industrial attachments
(m) Conduct skills gap analyses identifying workforce training needs
(n) Develop training curricula and competency standards for trades
(o) Certify trainees completing ITF skills programs
(p) Collaborate with industries on customized workforce training
(q) Support women and persons with disabilities skills training
(r) Provide mobile training reaching rural and underserved areas
(s) Coordinate with TVETIs, polytechnics and technical colleges
(t) Advance Nigeria's human capital development, reduce unemployment and build skilled industrial workforce supporting manufacturing, construction and economic diversification

Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC) is federal regulatory agency overseeing Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) and infrastructure concessions in Nigeria. Headquartered in Abuja, operating under Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission Act 2005 under Presidency. Established to regulate PPP projects ensuring value for money, fiscal sustainability and public interest protection. ICRC provides technical support to MDAs developing PPP projects. Conducts Outline Business Case (OBC) and Full Business Case (FBC) reviews approving projects. Issues Compliance Certificates for PPP projects meeting regulatory requirements. Monitors concession agreements implementation. Maintains PPP project database. Provides capacity building for MDAs on PPP procurement. Develops guidelines, regulations and standard templates for PPP contracts. Conducts Value for Money assessments ensuring taxpayers benefit from PPPs. Reviews unsolicited proposals from private sector. Addresses fiscal risks from government guarantees in PPPs. Promotes transparent, competitive PPP procurement. Has reviewed major projects including Lekki-Epe Expressway, Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 2 and others. Faces challenges from limited PPP financing, capacity gaps and slow project approvals.

**Core Mandate:** To regulate Public-Private Partnerships, ensure value for money, provide technical PPP support to MDAs, monitor concessions and promote sustainable infrastructure delivery through private sector participation.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Yaoundé, Cameroon, is Nigeria's primary diplomatic mission to Republic of Cameroon serving as embassy headquarters (note: separate consular offices may exist in Buea/Douala). mandate_description:
Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) is Nigeria's premier federal forestry research institution conducting comprehensive research on forest resources, forest ecology, conservation and sustainable management. Located in Ibadan, Oyo State in southwestern Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. FRIN conducts cutting-edge research on Nigerian forest ecosystems, indigenous tree species, forest genetics and breeding, forest products development, wildlife conservation and environmental protection. The Institute addresses Nigeria's catastrophic deforestation crisis with Nigeria losing approximately 350,000-400,000 hectares of forest cover annually representing 3.5-4% deforestation rate among world's highest. Research programs cover agroforestry systems integrating trees with agriculture, forest plantation establishment and management, non-timber forest products including mushrooms and honey, forest pests and diseases management, and climate change impacts on Nigerian forests. FRIN maintains valuable germplasm collections preserving endangered tree species, operates research forest stations across ecological zones and manages tree nurseries producing quality seedlings. Provides critical technical advice to Federal Ministry of Environment on national forest policy, legislation and conservation strategies. Trains forestry researchers, technicians and extension officers. Publishes research findings in scientific journals and technical bulletins disseminating forestry knowledge. Collaborates with international forestry organizations including FAO, IUCN and CIFOR.

**Core Mandate:** To conduct forestry research, develop sustainable forest management practices, conserve forest biodiversity, provide scientific basis for Nigeria's forest policy and address catastrophic deforestation crisis through research and innovation.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Conduct comprehensive forestry research on Nigerian forest ecosystems across ecological zones
(b) Research indigenous tree species characteristics, distribution, propagation and conservation
(c) Develop tree species improvement programs through genetics, breeding and selection
(4) Study forest ecology, forest dynamics, forest regeneration and succession patterns
(e) Research non-timber forest products including mushrooms, honey, fruits and medicinal plants
(f) Develop agroforestry systems integrating trees with crops for sustainable land use
(g) Research forest plantation establishment techniques, species selection and management practices
(h) Study forest pests and diseases developing integrated pest management strategies
(i) Research climate change impacts on Nigerian forests including carbon sequestration
(j) Develop sustainable forest management practices balancing conservation with utilization
(k) Maintain germplasm collections and gene banks preserving endangered Nigerian tree species
(l) Operate research forest stations across savanna, rainforest and montane ecological zones
(m) Research forest products processing, wood technology and value addition methods
(n) Study wildlife conservation, forest-wildlife interactions and habitat management
(o) Research forest soil science, forest nutrition and site productivity
(p) Provide technical advisory services to Federal Ministry of Environment on forest policy
(q) Train forestry researchers, technicians, extension officers and forestry students
(r) Publish scientific research findings, technical bulletins and forestry extension materials
(s) Disseminate forestry research knowledge to stakeholders including farmers and communities
(t) Collaborate with international forestry research organizations advancing scientific solutions to Nigeria's deforestation crisis threatening biodiversity, climate and livelihoods

French Language Village Badagry is a specialized federal institution providing immersive French language education and francophone cultural training. Located in Badagry, Lagos State near Nigeria-Benin border approximately 60 km west of Lagos, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. The Village creates total immersion learning environment where students, trainees and participants live and learn French language through intensive instruction, cultural experiences and constant interaction with francophone culture and native speakers. Addresses critical need for French language proficiency given Nigeria's anglophone status completely surrounded by francophone neighbors: Benin Republic to west, Niger Republic to north, Chad to northeast and Cameroon (partially francophone) to east. ECOWAS regional integration agenda requires French-English bilingual capacity for Nigerian leadership. The Village provides intensive French language courses from beginner to advanced proficiency, francophone cultural immersion programs, French teacher training for Nigerian secondary schools and specialized French courses for diplomats, military officers, business people and government officials preparing for engagement with francophone Africa. Promotes Nigeria-francophone West Africa mutual understanding addressing language barriers limiting Nigerian regional influence. Badagry's strategic location near Benin border facilitates authentic francophone cultural exposure and cross-border educational exchanges.

**Core Mandate:** To provide immersive French language education, promote francophone cultural understanding, develop French-English bilingual Nigerians and support regional integration and francophone Africa engagement.

(b) Create authentic francophone cultural environment facilitating natural language acquisition

(d) Promote deep understanding of francophone African cultures, societies, history and traditions
(e) Prepare Nigerian diplomats for Foreign Ministry postings in francophone countries worldwide
(f) Train Nigerian military and security officers for operations in francophone Sahel and West Africa
(g) Develop French-English bilingual capacity essential for Nigerian ECOWAS regional leadership
(h) Provide comprehensive French teacher training for Nigerian secondary school French teachers
(i) Offer intensive cultural immersion programs exposing participants to francophone African life
(j) Teach French literature, francophone history, French civilization and cultural studies
(k) Facilitate student exchange programs with francophone African educational institutions
(l) Provide internationally-recognized French language certification including DELF/DALF testing
(m) Train Nigerian government officials for engagement with francophone neighbors and international organizations
(n) Organize French language competitions, cultural festivals and francophone celebration events
(o) Develop French language teaching materials, textbooks and pedagogical resources
(p) Provide short-term intensive French crash courses for business people and professionals
(q) Promote Nigeria-francophone West Africa relations through linguistic and cultural bridges
(r) Address critical language barriers severely hindering Nigeria's West African regional leadership aspirations
(s) Coordinate with francophone embassies, Alliance Française and francophone cultural centers
(t) Advance Nigeria's ECOWAS leadership effectiveness and francophone Africa diplomatic engagement through systematic French language capacity development addressing anglophone isolation
